subject: Clarify billing units for split-context / stitched requests
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fincloud.com>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: priya.s@fincloud.com
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on how partial contexts and stitched requests are billed

Hi Alex,

Quick one from procurement as we parse your RFP: FinCloud has a workflow where we stitch multiple user turns and system prompts into a single long context, but often we also send short incremental requests that overlap with previously cached context (we do some client-side stitching and some server-side). Two specific questions: 

1) Do you bill per actual tokens processed on the backend or per request rounded up to some canonical chunk size? For example, if a request processes 350 tokens but your billing unit is a 128-token window, how is that arithmetic applied?

2) When we do incremental requests that reuse a cached prefix (e.g., we request for tokens 1001-1200 using an existing KV cache for 1-1000), do we pay for the whole 1200 token context or just the delta?

We're trying to model monthly spend and want to avoid surprises if overlapping context results in double-counting. I've attached a spreadsheet with sample request logs.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Procurement Manager, FinCloud
liam.oconnor@fincloud.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fincloud.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on how partial contexts and stitched requests are billed

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear examples and for the sheet. High level: we bill for the tokens our serving runtime actually decodes/encodes per request, but there are a few implementation details worth calling out so you can model costs precisely. Two quick notes up-front:

- We use a billing granularity we call a "billing chunk" (configurable per contract): requests are rounded up to the nearest chunk for invoicing, not per raw token.
- Cache reuse (prefix KV reuse) avoids re-processing those tokens on the model runtime, so you are not charged twice for identical KV that never gets re-decoded — but the behavior depends on how the requests are routed and whether the cached state is considered persistent across the request boundary.

I'll loop in Neha (SE) and Jonas (account lead) to add concrete examples from our side and to propose a contract clause that unambiguously covers: rounding behavior, how delta requests are measured, and how we handle batched/aggregated billing for bursty traffic.

– Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fincloud.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sinha <priya.s@fincloud.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on how partial contexts and stitched requests are billed

Thanks Alex — that helps. A couple follow-ups from Priya (technical ops):

- We use a mix of client-side stitching (client keeps a sliding window) and occasional full rehydration of the full context to different regions. If cache persistence is required to avoid double charges, what are the operational constraints? (sticky routing, session affinity, TTL on KV, etc.)

- For modeling: can you give an explicit numeric example with a common chunk size (say 128 tokens) showing three scenarios: full single-shot request (1200 tokens), incremental delta-only (send 200 tokens with KV for previous 1000), and overlapping incremental (send 300 tokens where 100 overlap with previous request)? We want to compare whether using client-side deltas vs single long requests materially changes cost.

Also, procurement asked if Redwood is willing to commit to a simpler billing rule in the SOW for committed volumes (e.g., bill actual used tokens rounded to nearest 64 up to a max per-request cap) — that would make forecast easier.

Best,
Liam

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on how partial contexts and stitched requests are billed

Hi Liam — Neha (SE) here. Below are the concrete examples you requested; I kept the math simple and used a billing chunk of 128 tokens for illustration. Assume per-token price p, but we'll keep it in tokens billed for clarity.

Example A — single-shot 1200-token request:
- Raw tokens: 1200
- Rounded to 128-token chunks: ceil(1200 / 128) = ceil(9.375) = 10 chunks => billed tokens = 10 * 128 = 1280

Example B — delta-only request where client sends 200 tokens and the server reuses KV for previous 1000 (no re-decode of the prefix):
- Server processes only the delta: 200 tokens
- Rounded: ceil(200 / 128) = 2 chunks => billed tokens = 2 * 128 = 256

Example C — overlapping incremental request where request includes 300 tokens but 100 tokens overlap with the server-side cache (server still needs to do some re-assembly but does not re-decode cached KV):
- Effective newly-decoded tokens = 300 - 100 = 200 (assuming overlap is recognized and skipped at decode time)
- Rounded: ceil(200 / 128) = 2 chunks => billed tokens = 256

Key operational notes:
- Overlap detection: if requests land on different hosts without shared KV or without a persistent cache store, the server may re-decode the shared prefix and you would be billed for the full context. To avoid that you can: enable session affinity (sticky routing), use our persistent KV store option, or include the minimal delta only in request payloads.
- Rounding policy: contract defaults to 128-token chunks, but for committed customers we can set a contract chunk size (64/128) and cap per-request rounding overhead (e.g., max rounding uplift of 10%).
- Aggregation and batching: for many small requests in the same minute, we offer an optional "aggregation window" (configurable) that can group requests for billing so the rounding overhead is amortized across the group. This is an add-on and typically included for Dedicated/Private customers.

I'll attach a quick CSV with the example calculations mapped to the rows in Liam's spreadsheet. Happy to jump on a short call to run through live logs.

– Neha
Neha Kapoor
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fincloud.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sinha <priya.s@fincloud.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on how partial contexts and stitched requests are billed

Neha — that's exactly the clarity we needed, thanks. Two quick asks before we finalize the SOW: 

1) For committed volume pricing (we're targeting ~450M tokens/mo), would Redwood agree to a 64-token contract chunk and a billing uplift cap of 8%? That would make our forecasts conservative.

2) If we enable session affinity and your persistent KV store in our Dedicated deployment, can you commit in the SOW that delta requests that reuse cache will not be billed for the prefix tokens (i.e., you will only bill newly-decoded tokens)? We'd like that as a formal guarantee with a short list of operational caveats (TTL, failover rehydration).

If you can confirm both items, procurement will prepare a redline-friendly SOW.

Regards,
Liam

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fincloud.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on how partial contexts and stitched requests are billed

Liam — appreciate the clear asks. We can commit to both items with the recommended caveats. Summary to include in the SOW: 

- Chunk size: 64-token billing chunk for committed volumes >= 400M tokens/mo.
- Billing uplift cap: 8% maximum rounding uplift per billing period (month) measured against actual decoded tokens for your account.
- Cache/delta guarantee: For Dedicated deployments with session affinity and Redwood persistent KV enabled, we will bill only for newly-decoded tokens when overlap is detected and the cache is successfully reused. Exceptions: failover rehydration, manual cache clears, or cross-region rehydration where cache is not present.

Next steps: I'll have our legalOps draft the SOW language and include an explicit definition and measurement method for the 8% uplift cap. Jonas will follow up on scheduling a short ops workshop to lock session affinity and TTL settings. Expect the SOW draft by EOD Friday.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
